findings.description: ensure_current opens then closes ordinary OS File descriptors on actual SQLite database inodes. On Unix DELETE transactions these close operations silently release SQLite process POSIX locks while SQLite still believes transaction active. New ensure_connections invokes this twice and therefore undermines the cross-process writer fence. Retained binding descriptor drop has same lifetime constraint.
findings.required: No transient DB inode descriptors opened/closed during any layout revalidation; use nofollow descriptor-relative metadata observation from retained parent dirs. Explicit bind/drop ownership must surround all SQLite connection lifetimes. Regression requires independent process DELETE contender before and after checks.
findings.resolution: All regular namespace entries (manifest/control/ledger) now use statat(SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW) from retained parent dirs and fstat on retained files. Manifest bytes use read_at on retained handle, with no cloning/opening/closing. Only DIRECTORY opens remain. Contract retains bind-before-SQLite-open and close-all-SQLite-before-layout-drop duty; owning runtime still pending. Independent5tests verify both DBs WAL/DELETE contention and alias refusal preserving locks.
